correctness.rationale: Commutation is proved generatorwise by maximal-letter-run counts. For \(N_i>1\) any multi-run image contradicts \(r(\Phi(w))=r(w)\) versus \(r(w^{N_i})>r(w)\); \(N_i=1\) forces letters of exponent one by length. Every root commutes with Phi and is monomial, even in exponent-one blocks by nonerasing monotonicity. Its letter transformation has finite order and is a permutation with cycle length \(d\) dividing \(k\). Cycle products yield \( (\prod e_i)^{k/d}=m \). The formal labeled-cycle formula counts all root assignments once. The provided checker exhaustively matches the formula and actual word composition in stated finite domains; a written proof handles universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: The recent primary literature motivates analysis of commutation and factorization in the whole endomorphism monoid. The result gives a natural complete centralizer classification for diagonal power maps on arbitrary finite alphabets, including the exceptional exponent-one submonoid. It derives a full positive-integer existence criterion, precise uniform coefficient enumeration of roots inside an infinite endomorphism monoid and nontrivial square-root obstructions, rather than an ad hoc numeric slice or routine restatement of a simple case.
